subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw pursue shared external session storage as a core storage backend/API, defer it behind the broader database-abstraction design, or route it outside core?
rationale: Current main still uses local path-backed session storage, but adding Redis/Mongo/Postgres-style shared storage changes config, credential handling, session/transcript lifecycle, migrations, consistency, and plugin/core ownership.

options.title: Defer to database abstraction
options.body: Keep this issue open as a session-specific requirement and resolve it after the broader networked database seam is designed.

options.title: Sponsor a session backend API now
options.body: Define a narrow core or plugin-facing session/transcript storage API with explicit migration and credential rules before implementation.

options.title: Reject core shared storage for now
options.body: Close the direction as out of current core scope and document deployment guidance such as sticky sessions or single-writer operation.

recommendation.title: Defer to database abstraction
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as a session-specific requirement and resolve it after the broader networked database seam is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman owns the closest session/transcript storage migration tracker and has the clearest adjacent implementation context for the session-specific boundary.
